mbm-2576.clue: The spoon stands up by itself.
mbm-2576.quote: My first ceramic spoon rest came out so narrow the spoon stood upright. My flatmates put a tiny paper flag on it. Now supper is served when the flag goes up.

mbm-2577.clue: I hear the turn in the ceiling.
mbm-2577.quote: My upstairs neighbors practice ballroom on Thursday nights. When they invited me up I already knew the squeaky turn in their waltz. I only had to learn what their feet were doing.

mbm-2578.clue: We let the tide erase the score.
mbm-2578.quote: I draw our volleyball points where the last wave stops. Whoever's ahead when the water wipes us clean gets first pick of the peaches. Close games taste sweeter.

mbm-2579.clue: My left turn has a ribbon on it.
mbm-2579.quote: When I finally linked turns on the practice slope, my sister tied a ribbon round my left pole. It flutters forward just before I plant it. The pole knows the turn now too.

mbm-2580.clue: I can tell fortunes with a postage stamp.
mbm-2580.quote: I tuck a duplicate stamp into a tiny envelope and ask a friend to name a country. My best trick was the time she named the wrong country and the postman actually came from there.

mbm-2581.clue: The counter with a crack runs faster.
mbm-2581.quote: My favorite board game piece split neatly in two. We decided it could leave one half to reserve a place and take the other half shopping. The game takes ages now but the town has a market.

mbm-2582.clue: I saved the sound of the grass.
mbm-2582.quote: After my first canopy landing I lay on the field listening to the grass move around my helmet. In the little log space for comments I wrote the name of the bird singing over me.

mbm-2583.clue: My sketchbook is full of picture frames.
mbm-2583.quote: I go to the museum for the paintings but keep getting distracted by their carved wooden edges. A tiny carved pear hiding in one frame took me three visits to draw properly.

mbm-2584.clue: The back of the quilt is a giant envelope.
mbm-2584.quote: I made a reading quilt with a big pocket behind it. My brother climbs under, reaches back and pulls out our next comic. It works best when I remember to fill it.

mbm-2585.clue: I catch the smallest scarf last.
mbm-2585.quote: I juggle two long red scarves and a tiny yellow one. The little one flutters onto my shoulder if I hold still. My nephew calls that the bird coming home.

mbm-2586.clue: My puppet keeps a pebble in his shoe.
mbm-2586.quote: I carved a wooden postman who kept leaning backward. A pebble in his shoe balanced him. Now he taps twice at every door and the audience can hear that the mail's arrived.

mbm-2587.clue: My canteen wears a tiny sweater.
mbm-2587.quote: My aunt knitted a sleeve for my hiking bottle. When a low cloud swallowed our ridge I could tell whose water I'd picked up without looking. Hers has the same stripes in reverse.

mbm-2588.clue: We slide one stone for the tea.
mbm-2588.quote: At the end of curling practice we aim our last stones at a chalk teacup near the button. Closest gets to pour. The ice maker always wins and takes his tea without milk.

mbm-2589.clue: The little airplane in my drawing goes up twice.
mbm-2589.quote: My niece asked where I came down after the jump. I showed her the landing field in my log. She drew a dotted line from the grass back to the plane in case I wanted another go.

mbm-2590.clue: My disc has a little door on the back.
mbm-2590.quote: I drew a mouse-sized front door on the underside of the family frisbee. When my nephew catches it he knocks before he throws it back. Whoever lives there travels very far.

mbm-2591.clue: I keep one blue tile in my notebook.
mbm-2591.quote: When they resurfaced our pool the caretaker gave me a loose tile. It holds the pages of my swim diary open. The wet little lines round it come from my hair after practice.

mbm-2592.clue: My lunch knows which slope I skied.
mbm-2592.quote: I pack two slices of bread around a ridge of cheese. A gentle run leaves the ridge intact. By the time I finish the moguls the cheese has explored every corner of the sandwich.

mbm-2593.clue: I stand on the crooked board first.
mbm-2593.quote: Our martial arts class takes place in the old dance hall. One board tips under my heel. I use that spot to practice a slow stance until the board stays still.

mbm-2594.clue: My quietest character lives in the margin.
mbm-2594.quote: I write mystery stories in longhand. On the edge of each page I draw the neighbor's cat watching the action. My friends flip through the cat before they'll read the crime.

mbm-2595.clue: The stumps make a fine picnic table.
mbm-2595.quote: When the beach cricket game finishes we lay a plank across our three short wooden stumps. My little brother deals the sandwiches from the neatest counter on the sand.

mbm-2596.clue: I can hear the old yellow one before I see it.
mbm-2596.quote: I collect the paint colors of the planes at our airfield in a tin of paper swatches. The old yellow trainer has two cards, sunshine above its wing and engine oil underneath.

mbm-2597.clue: I know the bow by its echo.
mbm-2597.quote: I train early enough to have the hall to myself. When I bow and clap my hands together the empty room answers once. Soon the kids come in and the room has plenty to say.

mbm-2598.clue: My flea-market list has just one button.
mbm-2598.quote: I carry the odd brass button from my grandpa's waistcoat in a box. On Saturdays I hunt for its twin. I've brought home three wrong buttons and four new friends.

mbm-2599.clue: I brought home a stairway in my pocket.
mbm-2599.quote: I rub pencil over the embossed railings on my travel postcards. One from a harbor stair has a repeating snail shape. I can climb all forty steps by moving my thumb.

mbm-2600.clue: My score pencil gets the tiny chair.
mbm-2600.quote: I made a dollhouse chair for my mini-golf pencil to rest on between scores. The course owner keeps it beside the last cup now. Even the shortest clubs get a clubhouse.
